And necessarily "and these" does not refer — or say the section of tzitzit is only according to one opinion; if so why does he challenge "why did Shema precede" [Tosafot Berakhot 14b s.v. "why" and Peri Chadash siman 67] — implies "and these" refers only to verses not sections; and lekhatchilah Chazal ordered them so as Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka said, etc. Nevertheless say rabbinically he does not fulfill; and Peri Chadash wrote: he was reading in the Torah, etc., and "and it shall be" before "or it shall be" of tzitzit — likewise not relevant to Keriat Shema; and therefore he fulfilled, not so Shema and "and it shall be" refer to it and "and these," etc. And this may be said as he wrote nearby that rabbinically he brings proof; however there is no proof, for one may say he fulfilled Shema and "and it shall be" and read tzitzit afterward and we teach "a mitzvah that requires," etc., or blessings, etc., and the like. If so, if he has two sections "Kadosh" and "and it shall be" and combines two sections of tefillin — if we say in doubt one may say doubt rabbinic to be lenient; and see Levush in Turei Zahav letter bet — requires further study. Return — Taz's view is like Levush that certainly the first verse — even if he does not know whether he said it or not, presumably establish the presumption and say that one — for all Israel recognize and know that intention is required in verse 1, only that he forgot now; and if you say what difference to us — say section 2 (wherever it can be clarified easily, etc.) — one may say it is like two domains; and necessarily we say in siman 63 letter gimel one reads in a whisper or waits with difficulty when he knows certainly he did not intend; not so here establish presumption — and see Lechem Mishneh chapter 2 of Keriat Shema halacha 14 — it seems so to Rambam: he returns to "and you shall love" but verse 1 establish presumption — see there (from what seems there regarding occasional reading he returns and reads in siman 63 seif 6 in Shulchan Aruch it is not clear if he did so that he should return and read — Beit Yosef according to his view here — understand). And Bach disagrees and Magen Avraham letter alef. חוזר עט״ז סברתו כלבוש דודאי פסוק ראשון אף שא״י אם אמר או לאו מסתמא אוקי אחזקה ואמר אותו דכל ישראל מכירים ויודעים שצריך כוונה בפסוק א׳ אלא ששכח עתה וכ״ת מאי איכפת לן יאמר פ״ב (כל היכא דאיכא לברורי בקל כו׳) י״ל דהוי כב׳ רשויות וע״כ אמרינן בסימן ס״ג אות ג׳ דקורא בלחש או ממתין מדוחק שיודע בודאי שלא כיון משא״כ כאן אוקי אחזקה ועיין לח״מ פ״ב מק״ש הי״ד נראה כן להר״מ חוזר לואהבת אבל פסוק א׳ אוקי אחזקה יע״ש (מה דמשמע שם דבקורא עראי חוזר וקורא בסי׳ ס״ג ס״ו בש״ע אין מבואר אם עשה כן שיחזור ויקרא דב״י לשיטתי׳ כאן והבן) והב״ח חולק ועמ״א א׳. ואני מסופק אם דילג פסוק בואהבת וגמר הפ׳ א׳ והיה א״ש אם יקרא אח״כ מדילוג וגומר הפרשה דקורא כסדר ומ״ש בנתיים והיה א״ש סדר פרשיות אין מעכב וצ״ע. ואם דילג תיבה בלבוש ופר״ח שיתחיל מתיבה ויגמור וא״ר אות ג׳ בשם מי״ט דיתחיל מראש הפסוק יע״ש:
peri_megadim.en:
What the author wrote in seif 61 — verses, and all the more words. And what he wrote "sections" — he has fulfilled is the view of Rambam in chapter 2 halacha 11 of Keriat Shema; and there is support, for if not so what does he say "why did Shema precede" — behold necessarily "and these"; and if you say it should precede, say then in truth how is this resolved? And necessarily "and these" does not refer — or say the section of tzitzit is only according to one opinion; if so why does he challenge "why did Shema precede" [Tosafot Berakhot 14b s.v. "why" and Peri Chadash siman 67] — implies "and these" refers only to verses not sections; and lekhatchilah Chazal ordered them so as Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka said, etc. Nevertheless say rabbinically he does not fulfill; and Peri Chadash wrote: he was reading in the Torah, etc., and "and it shall be" before "or it shall be" of tzitzit — likewise not relevant to Keriat Shema; and therefore he fulfilled, not so Shema and "and it shall be" refer to it and "and these," etc. And this may be said as he wrote nearby that rabbinically he brings proof; however there is no proof, for one may say he fulfilled Shema and "and it shall be" and read tzitzit afterward and we teach "a mitzvah that requires," etc., or blessings, etc., and the like. And for me the matter still requires a reason why in reading "and these" refers only to verses; and in writing in tefillin and mezuzah even sections out of order are invalid — see Yoreh De'ah 288 and Turei Zahav letter alef and here letter alef. And if we say likewise from the Torah it is valid and rabbinically invalid in writing — see Gemara Yomi chapter 1 of Tefillin letter nun: in reading since we see "and it shall be" at the end, Chazal were not particular; likewise bedieved. If so, if he has two sections "Kadosh" and "and it shall be" and combines two sections of tefillin — if we say in doubt one may say doubt rabbinic to be lenient; and see Levush in Turei Zahav letter bet — requires further study. And see Baer Heitev in the name of Erech Lechem; and with God's help it will be explained in Magen Avraham; and here there is no place to elaborate.
Return — Taz's view is like Levush that certainly the first verse — even if he does not know whether he said it or not, presumably establish the presumption and say that one — for all Israel recognize and know that intention is required in verse 1, only that he forgot now; and if you say what difference to us — say section 2 (wherever it can be clarified easily, etc.) — one may say it is like two domains; and necessarily we say in siman 63 letter gimel one reads in a whisper or waits with difficulty when he knows certainly he did not intend; not so here establish presumption — and see Lechem Mishneh chapter 2 of Keriat Shema halacha 14 — it seems so to Rambam: he returns to "and you shall love" but verse 1 establish presumption — see there (from what seems there regarding occasional reading he returns and reads in siman 63 seif 6 in Shulchan Aruch it is not clear if he did so that he should return and read — Beit Yosef according to his view here — understand). And Bach disagrees and Magen Avraham letter alef. And I am in doubt: if he skipped a verse in "and you shall love" and completed section 1 and "and it shall be" before Shema — if he reads afterward from the skip and completes the section, he reads in order; and what he wrote in the middle "and it shall be" before Shema — order of sections does not hinder — requires further study. מג"א ס"ק א' דחוזר לראש. דכיון דספק לו. ממילא ודאי לא כוון עיי"ש. וע' באשל אברהם רסי' צ"א דהקשה מההוא דספק התפלל אינו חוזר הא כיון דס"ס ממילא ודאי לא כיון דצריך לחזור ולהתפלל מדינא דהש"ס עיי"ש:

And in Kesef Mishneh I found it seems somewhat like the words of Levush — until here his language. However from Tosafot [Berakhot] 16a and Agudah and Semak and Avudraham it seems that even if he skipped a word he begins from the beginning of the verse.

kaf_hachayim.he: ג) שם אבל אם הקדים פ' לחברתה אעפ"י שאינו רשאי יצא. וכ"כ הפר"ח אות א' פרמ"ג במש"ז ריש הסי', ר"ז אות א', סידור בי"ע אות א' ועיין מש"ל סי' ס"א אות ט"ז בשם הכוו' שיש טעם בסוד להיות דוקא כסדרן יעו"ש. וכ"כ הרו"ח או' א' וכתב דצריך לחזור ולקרא יעו"ש:

(comment 3) That they are accustomed, etc. — and all the more so in "and you shall find," etc. Meaning: behold even in "and you shall write them" which implies that they are accustomed — he says "in order that they multiply" after the verse "and you shall write them" in the first section; and if so it implies he had not yet read only section one; nevertheless we say presumably he said in order also the second section; all the more so in another word.

mishnah_berurah.he: (ח) ואינו יודע - ומיירי שאינו זוכר כלל שום תיבה שאמר מפרשה שנייה וגם מיירי שעדיין לא התחיל תיבת ויאמר דאם אחר שהתחיל ויאמר עלה לו הספק על לבו תלינן דמסתמא אמר גם פרשה שניה כפי הרגלו:

And this is where one did not begin "so that your days shall be multiplied" [which immediately follows only in the second section], but if one did begin "so that your days shall be multiplied", there is no need to go back in that one can assume one followed one's routine and continued.

shaarei_teshuvah.he: וכתבתם עבה"ט ועיין בש"צ בשם מאמר מרדכי דבקורא והצבור עומד בוכתבתם השני' מלפניו או מאחריו יאמר וכתבתם שבשני' וכן לאידך גיסא אם התחיל למען ירבו והצבור עומד בוכתכתם הראשונ' דמוכח' מלתא שטעה ולאו סרכי' נקט ואזיל ע"ש:

turei_zahav.he: היה עומד בוכתבתם כו'. הא דלא נקט וקשרתם דאי' ג"כ בב' פרשיות שמעתי לתרץ בשם מהר"ל מפראג דאין לטעות שם דוקשרתם הראשון הוא בקמ"ץ והשני הוא בסגו"ל. ועדיין קשה למה לא נקט בשבתך בביתך שהוא ג"כ ב"פ בב' הפרשיות ונ"ל דאורחא דמלתא נקט לפי שאין דרך לטעות בתחלת פרשה ראשונה או באמצעה דודאי יוכל להרגיש לפי הזמן שהתחיל לקרות אם הוא עדיין בפרשה ראשונה או בפרשה השנייה אבל כשהוא קיים בסוף הפרשה הראשונה שיש קצת זמן ארוך שפיר יוכל לטעות דשמא סיים הפ' השניה לכן נקט טעה בוכתבתם שהוא סוף פ' ראשונה כנ"ל:
turei_zahav.en: He was standing in uchtavtem, etc. That which it did not mention ukshartem — because ukshartem also appears in both sections; I heard explained in the name of Maharal of Prague that one does not err there, for in ukshartem the first is with kamatz and the second with segol. And still it is difficult why it did not mention beshivtecha beveitekha, which also appears in both sections in both paragraphs; and it seems the manner of the matter — it mentioned according to what there is no way to err at the beginning of the first section or in its middle, for certainly one can tell by the time he began to read whether he is still in the first section or the second; but when he is at the end of the first section there is a somewhat long time, so one can well err that perhaps he finished the second section — therefore it mentioned erring in uchtavtem, which is the end of the first section, as stated.
